title: Ten metro areas in two years
lede: Webvan operated in one market for eleven months before opening a second. After the HomeGrocer merger it ran distribution centers in ten metro areas, and closed three of them in the first half of 2001.

figure.title: Webvan’s distribution network, 1999–2001
figure.whatItShows: every market Webvan served, the facility that served it, and when it closed. Press play or pick a date on the timeline: pins appear when a site opened and gray out when it closed.
figure.caption: Pins are placed at city level, and some are nudged apart so they don’t overlap; a thin line joins a moved pin to its true location. Facility sizes are from the 2000 10-K[^3]. Launch and closing dates are from the 10-K, 10-Q and press[^3][^7][^15]. Base map: U.S. Census Bureau via us-atlas[^29].

legend.label: On the 2001 auction list, never opened

pins.title: Oakland, CA: the first distribution center
pins.text: 340,000 sq ft, serving the Bay Area from June 1999, and Sacramento until early 2001.

pins.title: Sacramento, CA
pins.text: Served from Oakland. Listed on the Nov 2000 home page; service ended in early 2001.

pins.title: Suwanee, GA: Atlanta
pins.text: 350,000 sq ft. Opened May 2000; closed April 2001 with about 485 jobs cut.

pins.title: Carol Stream, IL: Chicago
pins.text: 355,000 sq ft, the largest center. Opened August 2000.

pins.title: Renton, WA: Seattle
pins.text: 110,000 sq ft, from HomeGrocer, which began in Seattle in June 1998.

pins.title: Portland, OR
pins.text: A HomeGrocer market from May 1999, served with Seattle.

pins.title: San Diego, CA
pins.text: 102,000 sq ft, from HomeGrocer (May 2000). First site moved to Webvan’s platform, Jan 2001.

pins.title: Carrollton, TX: Dallas
pins.text: From HomeGrocer, operating from May 2000. Closed February 2001; charge of up to $60.0M.

pins.title: Foster City, CA: headquarters
pins.text: About 113,000 sq ft of offices at 1241 E. Hillsdale Blvd.

pins.title: Kirkland, WA: offices
pins.text: HomeGrocer’s home; about 82,000 sq ft. About 400 jobs here and in Foster City were cut in April 2001.

pins.title: Las Vegas, NV: customer service
pins.text: The National Customer Service Center, 33,500 sq ft, listed in the 2000 10-K.

pins.title: Glen Burnie, MD
pins.text: On the October 2001 auction list. The prospectus planned a Washington, D.C. market; we found no record that it opened.

steps.label: Jun 1999
steps.title: The Bay Area store opens
steps.text: Commercial launch from the 340,000 sq ft Oakland center, designed for 8,000 orders a day. Headquarters is in Foster City.

steps.label: Nov 1999
steps.title: IPO at $15
steps.text: Still one market. The IPO raises $375M gross, and Bechtel is already contracted to build up to 26 more centers.

steps.label: May 2000
steps.title: Atlanta opens
steps.text: A 350,000 sq ft center in Suwanee, Georgia, the second market, while the Bay Area still loses money.

steps.label: Aug 2000
steps.title: Chicago opens
steps.text: A 355,000 sq ft center in Carol Stream, Illinois, the biggest in the network.

steps.label: Sep 2000
steps.title: HomeGrocer merger closes
steps.text: About $1.04B in stock adds Seattle, Portland, Los Angeles, Orange County, San Diego and Dallas, on a different technology platform. Sacramento also appears on the Nov 2000 city list.
steps.estimate: Sacramento’s launch date is not in our sources; it is shown from the merger, the first date we can place it.

steps.label: Feb 2001
steps.title: Dallas closes
steps.text: The ex-HomeGrocer Carrollton facility shuts after about nine months, with up to $60M in charges. Sacramento service ends in early 2001.

steps.label: Apr 2001
steps.title: Atlanta closes
steps.text: About 485 jobs there and 400 at headquarters and Kirkland. Cash is down to $115M.

steps.label: Jul 9, 2001
steps.title: Shutdown
steps.text: All deliveries stop in seven markets. About 2,000 workers are let go and 750,000 active customers lose the service.

steps.label: Oct 2001
steps.title: The auctions
steps.text: Court-approved auctions at ten facility sites and headquarters, including a Glen Burnie, Maryland site with no record of ever opening.

text: auction list. No record it opened.

blocks.title: Operating facilities in the 2000 10-K

blocks.body: Smaller “station” sites fed the large centers, and the 10-K doesn’t list them. The October 2001 auction list adds Azusa, Irvine and Kent, plus Glen Burnie, Maryland, which fits the planned Washington, D.C. market.[^1][^28] We found no evidence that Glen Burnie ever served customers.
